title: Vulva Anatomy: External Structures, Vestibule & Vessels
description: Study vulva anatomy on an honest external teaching plate, identifying the mons pubis, labia majora and minora, clitoral glans, vestibule, and nerve supply.
h1: Vulva Anatomy: External Genital Structures, Vestibule and Innervation
blurb: Honest surface anatomy of the external female genital region—mons pubis, labia majora and minora, clitoral glans, and separate urethral and vaginal openings.
lead: In anatomical terminology, the vulva refers specifically to the external genital structures visible on the perineal surface—distinct from the internal vaginal canal. In this illustrated guide to vulva external genital anatomy, we examine 20 documented structures—including mons pubis, labia majora, labia minora, clitoral glans & hood—linking regional topography, tissue architecture, physiological mechanisms, and clinical reasoning.
overview: In anatomical terminology, the vulva refers specifically to the external genital structures visible on the perineal surface—distinct from the internal vaginal canal. The vulva is the external genital region, not the internal vaginal canal. This cleaned surface teaching illustration shows the mons, labia, clitoral glans, vestibule and separate urethral and vaginal openings. Deeper glands, nerves and clitoral erectile tissue are described without a misleading surface pointer. Within the human body, the vulva — external genital anatomy (Vulva) is situated in external genital region / urogenital triangle, receives arterial perfusion via internal & external pudendal arteries, and is innervated by pudendal (S2–S4), ilioinguinal & genitofemoral branches.

Structurally, the mons pubis comprises fatty pad over pubic symphysis. Physiologically, the mons pubis cushions pubic bone. The labia majora (Labia majora pudendi) is outer skin folds containing fat and connective tissue. Physiologically, the labia majora protect the vestibule and inner folds. The labia minora (Labia minora pudendi) is inner hairless folds, highly variable in size and pigmentation. Physiologically, the labia minora governs border the vestibule and contribute to clitoral hood. Structurally, the clitoral glans & hood (Glans et preputium clitoridis) comprises glans at the anterior meeting of labia minora, under prepuce. Physiologically, the clitoral glans & hood governs highly innervated erectile tissue. Structurally, the vulvar vestibule (Vestibulum vaginae) comprises space between labia minora containing urethral and vaginal openings. Physiologically, the vulvar vestibule governs shared surface region for urinary and genital outlets. Structurally, the external urethral meatus (Ostium urethrae externum) comprises urinary opening anterior to vaginal introitus. Physiologically, the external urethral meatus governs urine exits here, not through the vagina.

Clinically, regarding the mons pubis, normal hair pattern and contour vary widely. From a diagnostic standpoint, in the labia majora, vulvar lymph largely drains to superficial inguinal nodes. In clinical pathology involving the labia minora, normal asymmetry is common and not pathological. Medical evaluation of the clitoral glans & hood also notes that clitoral neurovascular supply should be respected in vulvar surgery.

questions.question: What structures are included in the vulva?
questions.answer: The vulva is the external genital region: mons pubis, labia majora and minora, clitoral structures and the vestibule with urethral and vaginal openings. Some deeper glands, vessels and nerves are described separately. Structurally, the vulvar vestibule (Vestibulum vaginae) comprises space between labia minora containing urethral and vaginal openings. Physiologically, the vulvar vestibule governs shared surface region for urinary and genital outlets.

questions.question: Are the vulva and vagina the same structure?
questions.answer: No. The vulva refers to external genital anatomy; the vagina is an internal muscular canal extending from the cervix to the vaginal opening. The opening lies within the vulvar vestibule. Structurally, the external urethral meatus (Ostium urethrae externum) comprises urinary opening anterior to vaginal introitus. Physiologically, the external urethral meatus governs urine exits here, not through the vagina.

questions.question: How are the urethral and vaginal openings positioned?
questions.answer: The external urethral opening is typically inferior to the clitoral glans and superior to the vaginal opening within the vestibule. Their appearance varies normally, so a teaching illustration is not a diagnostic reference. The greater vestibular gland ducts is paired ducts open near the posterior part of the vestibule, lateral to the vaginal opening. Physiologically, the greater vestibular gland ducts governs convey gland secretions to the vestibular surface.

questions.question: What do the labia minora do?
questions.answer: The labia minora are inner hairless folds that border the vestibule and join anteriorly near the clitoral hood. Their size, color and asymmetry vary normally between people. The labia minora (Labia minora pudendi) is inner hairless folds, highly variable in size and pigmentation.

questions.question: Can the surface image show Bartholin glands or the clitoral crura?
questions.answer: No. The greater vestibular glands and most clitoral erectile structures lie below the surface. Their locations are described as deep study notes, not marked as visible on the external surface illustration. The clitoral body & crura (Corpus et crura clitoridis) is paired erectile corpora extend along pubic rami. Physiologically, the clitoral body & crura governs erectile engorgement.
